what_this_measures: That the support crop's decision margin is reported by the product's own reconstruct stage, and what it says on the record's own input. The figure existed inside the crop before this and was discarded, so a user could not tell whether the published reproducibility applied to their scan.
why_it_matters: The crop is a threshold on a per-vertex distance and the reconstruction under it is not reproducible. Whether its verdicts reproduce is therefore a fact about the caller's geometry, not a property of the rule, and crop-decision-stability.json says so explicitly: the condition to re-check elsewhere is the ratio, not the verdict.
executed: npa.workbench.open3d.runner.run_multiway then run_reconstruct, the entry points the workflow calls; no mirrored copy of the stage

reproducibility.what_that_means: 2 vertices sit closer to the threshold than vertices routinely move between runs (1e-05 m, the largest in 46 pair comparisons), so a rerun may return a different verdict for them and move the counts derived from it by up to 2 at that displacement -- and by up to 238 at the largest displacement ever recorded (0.002187 m), which is the figure to size an error bar from. May, not will: being inside the displacement makes a vertex able to cross, not likely to. A denser capture shortens the distances themselves. Changing --support-distance-factor moves the cut rather than the geometry, so it changes which vertices sit near it and is not reliably a reduction -- re-run and read this figure again.

measured_by.what_was_measured: repeated Poisson reconstructions of one fused cloud, comparing the occupancy decision at every scene voxel between pairs of runs: 46 pair comparisons at two capture densities for the routine figure, and one independent observation that did not reproduce in three further attempts for the worst recorded
measured_by.on_what_input: one scene -- the Open3D ICP demo fragments -- at voxel 0.05 and 0.02. Both figures are therefore properties of that scene's geometry and capture, not of the reconstruction algorithm in general.
measured_by.kind_of_figure: sample maxima. Each is the largest value observed in a finite number of comparisons, which is not the same as a bound on what can occur.
measured_by.published_as: crop-decision-stability.json in the Open3D evidence directory, alongside the stability study that produced it rather than alongside this field

reproducibility.what_no_verdict_here_establishes: Both displacement figures are the largest values seen in a finite number of comparisons on one scene, so they are sample maxima and not bounds. Nothing about Poisson reconstruction prevents a run from displacing a vertex further than either, and a scene with different geometry, scale or noise may well do so. Read every verdict here as 'against displacements that have been measured', including the strongest one. If a decision must hold rather than be likely to hold, the margin is the figure to act on, not the verdict.
reproducibility.what_a_displacement_means_here: Not the motion of a tracked vertex. A rerun calls Poisson again and derives its density threshold from that run's own density array, so the vertex set is regenerated rather than perturbed and no vertex can be followed between runs. The figures are nearest-point distances between two independently generated vertex sets, which is what makes them a statement about how sensitive a decision near the cut is, and not a count of vertices that can flip. A rerun can also introduce or drop vertices near the threshold, and the counts above do not bound that.

crop_margin.what_this_does_not_establish: That the reconstruction is correct. A vertex far from the cut can still be in the wrong place, and a reproducible verdict on an invented surface is still a verdict on an invented surface. This says only whether re-running would decide differently.

crop_margin.why_not: support cropping is disabled, so there is no threshold for anything to sit near

what_the_result_shows: On this input the verdict is not_guaranteed at both enabled factors, from a handful of vertices inside the routine displacement out of eighteen thousand. That is consistent with the 46 pair comparisons that found no cell changing its verdict: a vertex inside the displacement is able to cross, not likely to. The first version of this field had a single threshold and reported the same scan as not_guaranteed on the strength of the unreproduced outlier alone, which is a warning a reader would learn to ignore.
what_this_does_not_establish: Anything about whether the reconstruction is correct. Every figure here concerns whether a rerun would decide differently, and a reproducible verdict on an invented surface is still a verdict on an invented surface.

reproducibility.note: Registration and reconstruction are both nondeterministic, so the counts move between runs. The verdict and the orders of magnitude are what reproduce.
